chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
Dieting (al-himyah) is not leaving a thing entirely so that you do not eat it at all, but rather dieting is to eat from the thing and reduce (your consumption of it).

key_terms.أَصْلًا: Entirely or completely; in this context, meaning total abstinence.
key_terms.الْحِمْيَةُ: Dieting or dietary restriction; the act of limiting food intake.
key_terms.تُخَفِّفَ: To reduce or lighten; referring to reducing the quantity or frequency of consumption.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of dieting (himyah) according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarifies that true dietary restriction ('al-himyah') is not characterized by total abstinence, but rather by moderation and reducing the quantity of consumption. This hadith reflects the Shia emphasis on balance in physical health, aligning with the Prophetic tradition that the stomach should be divided into thirds for food, drink, and air, thereby rejecting extreme asceticism in favor of sustainable, moderate living.
